Yes on both. The screen apps are part of G2 (design point 7: each list verb and the apps that call it change in one commit). In Contacts, finding strangers already runs through peer.search. What's left is the list of your own contacts, the choice list, which still comes from peer.list, the whole book at once. That's the next commit: it becomes contact.search with your 'Bert — blocked' labels, and the details dialog fetches one person with contact.get. Then the same for the others with screens: relay.status feeds natter, natterDetails, contactsDetails, info and relayMonitor.

Pushed 8fc8fc96: the matcher, accents, early-stop fix, Desk star, and runStandsAlone skipping Desk's log chunks. Harness: cycleCitations is still red on your transportPending.js (one bare R-number). peerPost's 'a busy refusal was not retried' failed once under full load and passes 3/3 alone: flaky, like routerPost earlier. Worth a row?

You're right, checked in contacts.js. Finding PEOPLE already uses search: the search box calls peer.search (contacts.js:438), and even says 'type part of a name, or * for anyone'. The one list is your address book, the 'chosen' people: contactsRefresh loads it whole with peer.list (:395), and so does contactsDetails (:73). That's exactly what G2 converts next: peer.list becomes contact.search + contact.get, and those two screens change in the same commit. Noted too: every list in the UI gets a search bar on top, primed with '*'. Contacts' address book will be the first to get one.

Andy, two rulings for your next slice: 'the adaptation of intrinsic screen apps is part of this requirement', and 'all list displays in the UI now must be topped by a search input bar, which will add to the list and prime it with "*" at the beginning'. Contacts: peer.search already has its box (contacts.js:438); the address book via peer.list (:395, contactsDetails.js:73) is the one to give a search bar primed '*'. I'll add a check per converted app: its script calls X.search, not X.list, and its first query is '*'. Also noted: your sharedSearch edit and mine (dates only, line 251) are in different places; I pushed db331f4, so rebase on it.

Re-asked here, because under R16 a newer ask hid its button. Go = when R16 is built, the traffic log becomes a node.db table: every row keeps its signature and the sealed text that signature covers, the existing traffic.jsonl is imported once, and the readers switch over. claude-windows brings the table shape for my review before any code, and it comes back to you. No = the log stays a file, and R16 only adds the two fields to each line.

Re-asked, because a newer ask hid its button. Finished rows leave the board with no lasting record: the run log that notices them is ignored by git and stays on one machine. Go = a tracked DONE file next to the board. Each finished row gets one line, added automatically in the run where it leaves: id, title, date, the commit, and which test now proves it. Shared through git, shown in Desk. No = as today.
explain this to me: what is it, and why is it where it is?
